title: Fixed-scalar pro-etale root module and its scalar-extension tensors
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme, with small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $m>0$. Use the actual root module $\mu_{m,T}$ of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Define $M_{m,T}$ as its fixed-$\mathbf Z/m$ presentation: restrict scalars to constant sections by [def-sfb-constant-ring-module-restriction], then along the inverse of the canonical universe-lift ring isomorphism. Its underlying sections and restrictions are the same roots as before. Let $A$ be any commutative ring with $mA=0$, in universe $u+1$ when $T$ is in universe $u$. Use the canonical scalar homomorphism $\mathbf Z/m\to A$ of [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. Define $D_{m,A,T}$ by extending each module of sections of $M_{m,T}$ along this homomorphism, then sheafifying [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; this is the balanced root tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For every pro-etale test $W$, $a\in A$ and root $z\in\mu_{m,T}(W)$, define $g_W(a,z)$ to be the image of $a\otimes z$ under that sheafification unit. These are the existing finiteRootProModule, finiteRootProTensor and finiteRootProGenerator, with the $A$ factor first. No finiteness, invertibility of $m$ on $T$, or flatness hypothesis is imposed.
